questions.q: A radio station in Enugu invites listeners to call in and vote on whether the state should ban commercial motorcycles from the city centre. Which limitation of the resulting public opinion report is most evident?
options: It measures the opinion of government officials rather than citizens.
It is collected too quickly to be regarded as public opinion.
It is based on a self-selected sample that may not represent all residents.
It cannot influence policy because it is not conducted by INEC.
questions.explanation: Call-in participants choose themselves, so the report reflects mainly the views of listeners who feel strongly enough to respond, not necessarily the whole adult population. A quick survey can still be useful, and INEC does not have to conduct every opinion poll for it to influence policy.

questions.q: A Lagos-based civil society group wants its survey on residents’ views about waste collection to have the greatest chance of influencing the state House of Assembly. Which action best uses public opinion responsibly?
options: Publish only comments from residents who already agree with the group.
Ask market leaders to announce the group’s preferred policy as the residents’ view.
Threaten to prevent lawmakers from holding sittings unless the policy is adopted.
Present a representative survey report to lawmakers during a public hearing.
questions.explanation: A representative survey gives lawmakers evidence about the views of the wider population, and a public hearing is a lawful channel for presenting it. Selecting only supportive comments, presenting one group's preference as everyone's view, or using threats distorts public opinion and undermines democratic participation.

questions.q: The monthly sharing of revenue from the Federation Account among the federal, state and local governments in Nigeria is handled by the
options: National Economic Council.
Federation Account Allocation Committee.
Federal Character Commission.
Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission.
questions.explanation: The Federation Account Allocation Committee brings together federal and state finance officials to share the revenue that enters the Federation Account each month. The Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission advises on the sharing formula and monitors accruals, but it does not carry out the monthly distribution itself.

questions.q: A state governor proposes to establish a state police command to tackle kidnapping. Why is this proposal constitutionally difficult under the 1999 Constitution?
options: State governments can only deploy soldiers for internal security.
The National Assembly cannot make laws on police matters.
Local government councils are solely responsible for policing in Nigeria.
The police are on the Exclusive Legislative List, so only the federal government can legislate on a national police force.
questions.explanation: Under the 1999 Constitution, policing is generally a federal matter listed in the Exclusive Legislative List; states may support security arrangements but cannot establish their own general police commands without constitutional change. Soldiers are not a substitute for police, and local governments do not have sole policing powers.

questions.q: The federal character principle in Nigeria is designed mainly to
options: allow each state to conduct its own foreign policy.
give the federal government control over all state resources.
ensure that appointments and public institutions reflect the diversity of the country.
make all public offices elective at the local government level.
questions.explanation: The principle seeks fair representation of Nigeria’s different states, ethnic groups and sections in federal institutions so that no group is systematically excluded. It does not grant states foreign-policy powers or make all public appointments elective.

questions.q: The Willink Commission of 1957 was set up primarily to
options: investigate the fears and demands of minority groups in Nigeria.
recommend a new revenue allocation formula for the regions.
draft Nigeria’s first independence constitution.
review the creation of local government areas in the North.
questions.explanation: The Willink Commission examined the fears expressed by minority ethnic communities about domination in the regions and considered possible safeguards. It did not draft the independence constitution or create local government areas.

questions.q: Which Nigerian constitution first included a chapter on Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy?
options: 1946 Richards Constitution.
1954 Lyttleton Constitution.
1979 Constitution.
1922 Clifford Constitution.
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy, setting out policy goals such as justice and public welfare, while usually making them non-justiciable. The earlier colonial constitutions did not contain this chapter.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is best classified as a promotional pressure group in Nigeria?
options: Trade Union Congress.
Nigerian Medical Association.
Civil Liberties Organisation.
National Union of Road Transport Workers.
questions.explanation: A promotional pressure group seeks to advance a general cause or value, such as human rights, rather than only the immediate interests of a particular occupation. The medical association, trade union congress and transport workers’ union are mainly sectional groups protecting their members’ occupational interests.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary function of a political party in a democracy?
options: Deciding all election petitions and disputes.
Enforcing court judgments against party members.
Registering voters and issuing permanent voter cards.
Aggregating different interests and presenting a clear programme to voters.
questions.explanation: Political parties bring together various interests, develop policy programmes and seek popular support through elections. Voter registration is handled by INEC, while election disputes are decided by tribunals and courts, not by parties.

questions.q: Which of the following is a defining feature of a unitary system of government?
options: Component units may secede from the central government under the constitution.
Ultimate legal authority is vested in one central government.
Powers are permanently divided between central and regional governments.
The central government is created by the component units and depends on their consent.
questions.explanation: In a unitary system, the central government is supreme and may delegate authority to local units without permanently sharing constitutional power. Permanent division of powers describes a federal system, while central dependence on component units describes a confederal arrangement.

questions.q: A republican form of government is best distinguished by the fact that its head of state
options: is an elected or appointed president rather than a hereditary monarch.
serves for life unless removed through a military coup.
exercises no ceremonial functions in the political system.
must always be chosen by the legislature rather than by the electorate.
questions.explanation: A republic has a non-hereditary head of state, usually chosen directly or indirectly by the people. The method of selection and the scope of the president's powers vary, so a republic is not defined by always being chosen by the legislature or by having no ceremonial role.

questions.q: During a constituency election in Oyo State, 250,000 voters were registered. If 72% of the registered voters turned out and 5% of the votes cast were invalid, how many valid votes were recorded?
questions.explanation: The number of votes cast is 250,000 × 0.72 = 180,000. Deducting 5% of 180,000 as invalid gives 180,000 × 0.95 = 171,000 valid votes.

questions.q: Under a closed-list proportional representation system, voters in a national election cast their ballots mainly for
options: a party's presidential candidate, who then appoints all legislators from the party.
a political party, with candidates elected according to the party's pre-arranged list.
individual candidates, whose order is ranked by the voters in multi-member constituencies.
a single candidate in a constituency, with the highest scorer winning the seat.
questions.explanation: In a closed-list proportional representation system, the party's list determines the order in which candidates take seats, and voters cannot alter that order. Ranking individual candidates describes systems such as the single transferable vote or open-list arrangements, not a closed list.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the legal effect of most resolutions adopted by the United Nations General Assembly?
options: They are not legally binding on member states, though they carry political and moral weight.
They are subject to a veto by the permanent members before they can be adopted.
They automatically become binding on all member states after adoption.
They may authorise the use of armed force without any action by the Security Council.
questions.explanation: General Assembly resolutions are generally recommendations and do not create binding legal obligations for member states. Enforcement matters and binding decisions under the Charter mainly rest with the Security Council, where the permanent-member veto applies.

questions.q: Which organ of the African Union is composed of heads of state and government and is its supreme decision-making body?
options: The Pan-African Parliament
The Peace and Security Council
The African Union Commission
The Assembly
questions.explanation: The African Union Assembly brings together heads of state and government and is the supreme organ of the Union. The Commission serves as the secretariat, while the Peace and Security Council handles conflict and security matters.

questions.q: Which ECOWAS institution is responsible for interpreting the community's treaties and settling disputes arising from their application?
options: The ECOWAS Commission
The ECOWAS Parliament
The Community Court of Justice
The Authority of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The Community Court of Justice performs the judicial function of ECOWAS, including treaty interpretation and dispute settlement. The Authority is the supreme political organ, the Parliament is consultative, and the Commission serves as the executive secretariat.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The practice whereby ministers in a parliamentary system are drawn from the legislature and remain answerable to it is best described as
options: devolution.
judicial review.
separation of powers.
fusion of powers.
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive is formed from the legislature and is accountable to it, so the two branches are fused rather than strictly separated. Judicial review concerns the courts' power over legislation, while devolution transfers powers to regional bodies.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Which constitutional arrangement best safeguards judicial independence in Nigeria?
options: Judges are appointed by the executive and serve at the pleasure of the president.
The National Assembly can reverse any court judgment by an ordinary resolution.
The judiciary must obtain clearance from the Ministry of Justice before hearing political cases.
Judges may be removed only through a prescribed procedure involving appropriate bodies, not by a simple executive order.
questions.explanation: Security of tenure and a special removal process protect judges from political pressure, which is essential to judicial independence. Service at executive pleasure, prior political clearance, and simple legislative reversal would all undermine that independence.

questions.q: Aminu, a Nigerian career diplomat, is posted to the High Commission in Accra. Which institution is directly responsible for coordinating his posting and the day-to-day conduct of Nigeria’s foreign relations?
options: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Nigerian Immigration Service
National Assembly
Federal Ministry of Interior
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, headed by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, coordinates Nigeria’s diplomatic missions, postings and day-to-day external relations. The Immigration Service handles border and migration matters, while the National Assembly legislates and oversees rather than conducts diplomacy.

questions.q: The Auditor-General of the Federation submits an annual report on public accounts. In the National Assembly, the report is normally examined by the
options: Public Accounts Committee
Rules and Business Committee
Appropriations Committee
Public Petitions Committee
questions.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee of each chamber examines the Auditor-General’s reports on how public funds have been spent. The Appropriations Committee deals mainly with budget estimates, while the Public Petitions Committee handles citizens’ complaints.

questions.q: A constitution that can be amended by the same ordinary legislative procedure used to make ordinary laws is best described as
options: an unwritten constitution
a federal constitution
a rigid constitution
a flexible constitution
questions.explanation: A flexible constitution can be altered through the ordinary law-making process, unlike a rigid constitution that requires special procedures such as a referendum or supermajority. Whether a constitution is federal or unwritten does not by itself determine how easily it can be amended.

questions.q: Between 1966 and 1975, the highest policy-making body of Nigeria’s military government was the
options: Federal Executive Council
National Assembly
Supreme Military Council
Council of State
questions.explanation: During that period, the Supreme Military Council was the supreme governing organ that took major policy decisions, while the Federal Executive Council served more as an administrative cabinet. The National Assembly had been suspended and decree rule replaced ordinary legislation.

questions.q: Nigeria’s foreign policy is often described as Afrocentric. This means that Nigeria
options: aligns only with former colonial powers
places Asian trade above African unity
avoids diplomatic relations with countries outside Africa
gives special priority to African issues in its external relations
questions.explanation: Afrocentric diplomacy makes Africa the centre of Nigeria’s foreign policy, especially through support for decolonisation, African unity and regional cooperation. It does not mean cutting off relations with non-African states.

questions.q: In Nigeria’s judicial system, the body that recommends suitable persons for appointment as judges and advises on judicial matters is the
options: Federal Character Commission
National Judicial Council
Nigerian Bar Association
National Judicial Institute
questions.explanation: The National Judicial Council plays the central constitutional role in recommending judicial appointments and handling related disciplinary matters. The Nigerian Bar Association is a professional body, while the National Judicial Institute mainly provides training for judicial officers.

questions.q: When a proposed constitution is submitted to the electorate and approved directly by them at a referendum, that approval is known as
options: amendment
ratification
judicial review
promulgation
questions.explanation: Ratification is the formal approval of a proposed constitution or constitutional change by the people or their authorised representatives. Amendment refers to changing an existing constitution, not the initial approval of a draft by referendum.

questions.q: For most of the period of military rule in Nigeria, political parties were
options: used to elect members of the Supreme Military Council
allowed to control the armed forces
banned or tightly controlled by the military government
given full freedom to compete for power
questions.explanation: Military regimes usually suspended or restricted party politics, arguing that civilian politicians had caused instability. Political parties were not used to elect the ruling military councils, whose members came from the armed forces.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of a rigid constitution is that it
options: is always unwritten and based only on conventions
prevents courts from interpreting constitutional provisions
can be changed by a simple majority in the legislature
can make necessary reforms difficult to achieve
questions.explanation: Because a rigid constitution requires special procedures such as referendums or special majorities, it can slow down or block reforms that are urgently needed. It is not necessarily unwritten, and courts still interpret its provisions.

questions.q: When a duly elected council chairman is prevented from entering his office by a crowd but civil servants still obey his written directives, the situation best illustrates that
options: sovereignty belongs to any group that gains control of public buildings
legitimacy automatically disappears once a public office is physically blocked
federal character is determined by physical control of local offices
authority rests on the right to govern, while power is the capacity to compel compliance
questions.explanation: The chairman's election and oath of office confer lawful authority, so staff still follow his directives. The crowd may have physical power, but it lacks the right to govern; legitimacy is not lost merely because an office is blocked.

questions.q: A military administration controls the police and army, but most citizens refuse to obey its laws and regard it as unlawful. This situation best shows that the administration has
options: sovereignty without authority
authority without power
power without legitimacy
legitimacy without power
questions.explanation: The administration has coercive power through the security forces but lacks popular acceptance as a rightful government. Legitimacy is about acceptance and lawful authority, not merely control of force.

questions.q: Which action best demonstrates Nigeria's external sovereignty?
options: Collecting taxes from residents of the Federal Capital Territory
Conducting local government elections under the 1999 Constitution
Entering into a bilateral trade agreement with another country in its own name
Creating new local government areas by a state law
questions.explanation: External sovereignty is the state's independence from external control, including the capacity to enter into relations and agreements with other states in its own name. The other actions are exercises of internal governmental powers within Nigeria.

questions.q: A civil society group in Enugu sponsors radio debates and town-hall meetings to persuade residents to support a proposed state health insurance law. This activity is best described as
options: performing diplomatic representation for the state
exercising judicial review of legislation
conducting the adjudication of electoral disputes
mobilising public opinion to influence legislation
questions.explanation: The group is shaping and expressing citizens' views so as to influence lawmakers, which is a form of public opinion activity. Judicial review, diplomacy and election dispute adjudication belong to courts or officials, not a civil society campaign.

questions.q: The constitutional provision specifically designed for a foreign woman married to a Nigerian citizen is acquisition of citizenship by
options: naturalisation
descent
birth
registration
questions.explanation: Nigerian citizenship by registration covers a woman married to a Nigerian citizen, subject to the constitutional requirements. Naturalisation is the general route for other foreigners, while descent and birth relate to different circumstances of acquiring citizenship.

questions.q: Which of the following matters is generally treated as a residual matter and therefore left to state governments in Nigeria?
options: Defence and the armed forces
Chieftaincy and traditional institutions
Currency and coinage
Citizenship and naturalisation
questions.explanation: Residual matters are those not listed in the exclusive or concurrent legislative lists, and chieftaincy matters fall in that category. Currency, defence and citizenship are exclusive federal matters.

questions.q: The Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission is important in Nigerian federalism because it
options: prepares the annual budget of the federal government
conducts elections into local government councils
recommends a formula for sharing the Federation Account among the tiers of government
appoints judges of state high courts
questions.explanation: The commission advises on revenue allocation and reviews the sharing formula among the federal, state and local governments. Elections, judicial appointments and budget preparation are handled by other institutions.

questions.q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is historically important in Nigeria because it
options: made Nigeria a republic within the Commonwealth
divided Nigeria into three regions with separate premiers
introduced the elective principle into the Legislative Council for Lagos and Calabar
created the office of Prime Minister with executive powers
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution introduced limited elections into the Legislative Council, with elected representation associated with Lagos and Calabar. The offices of Prime Minister and a republican presidency came later, while the regional division is linked to the Richards Constitution.

questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is notable in Nigeria's constitutional history because it
options: provided for Nigeria's immediate independence
created a republic with an elected President as Head of State
divided Nigeria into the Northern, Western and Eastern regions
introduced the elective principle for the first time
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution established three regions and regional legislatures, which marked an important step in the country's constitutional development. The elective principle was introduced earlier by the Clifford Constitution, while the republic came in 1963.

questions.q: In Abuja, the Nigerian Bar Association issues a public statement opposing a proposed law that would weaken the independence of the judiciary. This action is best described as
options: a political party nominating a candidate for election
a legislature exercising its oversight powers
a professional association trying to influence public policy
an electoral commission delimiting constituencies
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Bar Association is a professional pressure group, and its statement aims to influence government policy without contesting elections. Political parties nominate candidates for electoral competition, while delimitation and oversight are functions of different institutions.

questions.q: When a political party conducts a vote among its members to select its candidate for an upcoming general election, the exercise is called
options: a primary election
a by-election
a general election
a referendum
questions.explanation: Primary elections are intra-party contests used to choose a party's candidate for a general election. By-elections fill vacant public offices, while referendums ask voters to decide specific issues.

questions.q: The practice whereby a ruling party in Nigeria rewards loyal members with appointments and contracts is best described as
options: political patronage
party primaries
internal democracy
judicial review
questions.explanation: Political patronage involves using state resources or appointments to reward supporters and loyalists of a ruling party. Internal democracy concerns open and fair decision-making within a party, not the distribution of rewards by a government.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a constitutional monarchy?
options: The monarch is elected by the armed forces.
The monarch controls all arms of government personally.
The monarch rules without any legal limitation.
The monarch's powers are limited by a constitution and are largely ceremonial.
questions.explanation: Under a constitutional monarchy, the constitution limits the monarch's powers, and the monarch usually performs ceremonial duties while elected officials govern. A monarch ruling without legal limits describes absolute monarchy, not constitutional monarchy.
